subsystems.name: Structural ring
subsystems.role: the load-bearing hoop that spins to create artificial gravity; its inner surface is the habitable floor.
parts: spokes or tension members to a central hub
segmented shell built from strong fibres

subsystems.name: Atmosphere retention walls
subsystems.role: hold the air in at the open edges of the ring without a roof.

subsystems.name: Landscape and soil
subsystems.role: the living surface: soil, water bodies, crops and settlements.

subsystems.name: Sunlight and day-night system
subsystems.role: brings natural light into an open ring and creates a day-night cycle.

subsystems.name: Spin and stability control
subsystems.role: keeps the ring turning at the right rate and corrects wobbles.

subsystems.name: Life support and ecology
subsystems.role: closes the loops for air, water and waste so the habitat can support people indefinitely.

buildSteps.title: Source materials in space
buildSteps.detail: Mine asteroids or the Moon for carbon, metals and volatiles, avoiding the cost of launching mass from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Make ultra-strong material
buildSteps.detail: Produce carbon nanotubes or graphene fibres in bulk, then weave or wind them into structural cables and sheets strong enough to carry the hoop tension.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the ring in segments
buildSteps.detail: Build curved sections in orbit and join them into a complete ring hundreds of kilometres in radius, using automated assembly and welding.

buildSteps.title: Spin the ring up
buildSteps.detail: Apply gentle, sustained thrust or use magnetic couplings to bring the ring to the rotation rate that gives about 1 g at the floor.

buildSteps.title: Raise the atmosphere walls
buildSteps.detail: Fit tall rim walls around the open edges, seal them, and begin filling the interior with air.

buildSteps.title: Add soil, water and life
buildSteps.detail: Spread soil, fill lakes and rivers, and introduce plants, microbes and eventually animals to build a working ecosystem.

buildSteps.title: Install the light system
buildSteps.detail: Deploy mirrors or shades that direct sunlight onto the inner surface and create a regular day-night cycle.

buildSteps.title: Commission and settle
buildSteps.detail: Test life support, stability and safety systems, then move in the first residents and expand the settlement.

prerequisites.why: no known bulk material can yet withstand the hoop tension of a ring this size while staying light enough to spin.
the structure is far too large to launch from Earth; it must be built in orbit from space-sourced materials.
current systems on the ISS recycle some air and water, but not enough for a self-sustaining city-sized habitat.
supplying thousands of tonnes of carbon and metal in orbit requires mining and refining off Earth.
small centrifuges have been tested on the ISS, but no large spinning habitat has ever been built or lived in.

pathway.milestone: research on carbon nanotubes and small rotating experiments in low Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: basic data on strength, materials behaviour and human comfort in artificial gravity.

pathway.milestone: in-space manufacturing and assembly of large structures from asteroid or lunar material
pathway.unlocks: the ability to build big things without launching them from Earth.

pathway.milestone: a small rotating habitat, such as an O'Neill cylinder, housing hundreds or thousands of people
pathway.unlocks: proof that closed ecosystems and spin gravity can work at scale.

pathway.milestone: a full Bishop Ring hundreds of kilometres in radius
pathway.unlocks: a self-sustaining artificial world with a land area comparable to a small country.
